Telem
TEE-lem
proper noun
Hebrew telem, perhaps “oppression” or “a furrow,” a town in the uttermost south of the hill country of Judah.

📖 Biblical Definition

Telem was a town reckoned in the uttermost part of the tribe of Judah toward the coast of Edom, numbered among the cities of the south country in the great roll of Judah’s inheritance (Jos 15:24). It is named once and named no more, set down with Ziph and Telem and Bealoth among the towns of the dry southland where the herdsmen of Judah pastured their flocks far from the great places of the kingdom. The dictionary does not labour to recover what Scripture has left brief; what it honours is that the Holy Ghost, who moved the men who wrote the book of Joshua, did not think this little southern town too small to be written in the record of the land. The lines were fallen unto Judah in pleasant places, and the bounds of their habitation were not the work of chance, but of the same God who divided to the nations their inheritance and set the bounds of the people (Deu 32:8; Act 17:26). Telem stands as a witness that the LORD numbers the least of His gifts. He who told the stars and called them all by name also wrote down the towns of the south country, that His people might know their portion was measured out by no careless hand. No corner of the heritage is forgotten of Him who gave it, and no saint’s portion is too obscure for His care.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A town in the uttermost south of the hill country of Judah, named among the cities of the south.

TELEM, a town in the uttermost part of the tribe of Judah toward the south.

It is named with Ziph and Bealoth among the cities of the south country.

It lay in the dry southland of Judah, toward the coast of Edom.

The name occurs once in the great roll of Judah’s inheritance.

It witnesses to the LORD’s exact apportioning of the land by lot.

📖 Key Scripture

Jos 15:24 — "Ziph, and Telem, and Bealoth,"

Psa 16:6 — "The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage."

Deu 32:8 — "When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel."

Act 17:26 — "And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A place of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses to the LORD’s sovereign apportioning of every saint’s portion.

expand to see more

Telem is a town of the sacred geography, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine it. The dictionary records it that the reader who meets the name in the cities of the south may know it for a real place in a real inheritance, given by a real God to a real people.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the faithfulness of God in the least things. He who set Telem in the uttermost south of Judah did not count it too small to be written. The saint who feels his portion hidden and unsung may remember this town, named once and then for ever silent in the page, yet kept in the book of God’s faithful dividing of the land.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “oppression” or “a furrow,” Telem names a southern town of Judah’s allotment.

The town toward the coast of Edom in the dry southland.

The name occurs but once in the book of Joshua.

Usage

"Like Telem in the south of Judah, no portion of the saint’s heritage is too small for the care of God."

"The LORD who numbered the towns of the southland numbers also the days and the gifts of His people."

"A name spoken once and no more is yet written for ever in the record of God’s faithful dividing."
